summary: We developed AstroTwin, a fully offline, deterministic Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) designed for Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO). On deep-space missions, progressive communication delays render real-time Earth telemedicine impossible. AstroTwin addresses this critical vulnerability by empowering non-physician astronauts to independently monitor, diagnose, and treat medical anomalies.   Our solution ingests vital telemetry from wearable edge nodes and integrates real-time NASA space weather data (DONKI) and biological baselines (OSDR). The system's Multi-Stressor Synergy Engine evaluates compounded spaceflight hazards—such as radiation spikes combined with elevated cabin CO2. Using a LangGraph state machine paired with local LLMs (Ollama), AstroTwin instantly generates context-aware triage protocols and cross-references a PostgreSQL medical inventory to prescribe safe treatments.Astronauts interface with the system through an interactive 3D Anatomical Bio-Twin, ensuring that life-saving, step-by-step medical guidance is always accessible without requiring an Earth uplink.
details:
AstroTwin is a fully offline, deterministic Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) built for deep-space missions. It acts as an autonomous medical officer during communication blackouts. The system ingests physiological telemetry (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure) from simulated wearable edge nodes (like the Tempus Pro) and environmental data. It runs this data through our Multi-Stressor Synergy Engine, which calculates the compounded risk of overlapping spaceflight hazards (e.g., microgravity + radiation + elevated CO2).

If an anomaly is detected, a deterministic LangGraph state machine routes the data through a local LLM (Ollama) and a ChromaDB vector database loaded with NASA Human Research Program (HRP) protocols. It instantly outputs step-by-step triage instructions mapped directly onto an interactive 3D Anatomical Bio-Twin, guiding non-physician astronauts through self-assessments and treatments.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact?

The primary benefit is Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO). Currently, deep-space missions face life-threatening vulnerabilities due to signal delays and blackouts. AstroTwin empowers astronauts to instantly monitor, diagnose, and treat themselves without waiting for Mission Control. The intended impact is to vastly increase crew survivability, preserve mission readiness, and automate complex medical logistics (like tracking radiation-degraded medication) in hostile environments.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Our stack is designed to run entirely locally on a simulated isolated spacecraft server cluster (tested on a Linux environment):

  • Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js (@react-three/fiber) for the interactive 3D Bio-Twin. AG Grid handles the dense telemetry visualization.
  • Backend & AI: Python, FastAPI, and LangGraph (for deterministic medical workflows). We use Ollama for local, offline-first LLM inference and ChromaDB for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Database: PostgreSQL (via SQLAlchemy) to track the spacecraft's medical inventory and calculate pharmacokinetic degradation.
  • NASA APIs: We programmatically query the NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository) for biological baselines (OSD-288, OSD-817) and the NASA DONKI API for live space weather (Coronal Mass Ejections).

How is your project creative?

AstroTwin takes a highly creative approach to aerospace medicine by moving beyond single-metric alerts:

  1. Multi-Stressor Synergy: Instead of just alerting for "high CO2," our engine calculates the combinatorial effects of spaceflight. For example, if it detects high radiation and microgravity, it dynamically generates a unique triage protocol for compounded cellular damage.
  2. Hub-and-Spoke Edge AI: We creatively simulated hardware constraints. Wearables lack GPUs, so we built a lightweight TinyML edge node script that only triggers the heavy, power-intensive LangGraph/LLM "Hub" when critical thresholds are breached.
  3. The "Judge's Sandbox": We built a dedicated, gamified control panel allowing users to manually drag sliders (Cabin CO2, Radiation, Sleep, Days in Space) to watch the 3D Bio-Twin and LangGraph AI dynamically rewrite triage protocols in real-time.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Pharmacokinetic Stewardship: Medications degrade faster in space due to radiation. We factored this into our PostgreSQL medical kit database—our AI will not prescribe a drug if its potency has degraded past safe levels based on mission duration and radiation exposure.
  • AI Hallucinations in Healthcare: We considered the danger of generative AI in medicine. We mitigated this by wrapping our LLM in a rigid LangGraph state machine, ensuring the AI can only summarize pre-approved NASA protocols and cannot invent phantom medications or dosages.
